A 22-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department with complaints of fatigue, shortness of
breath, and palpitations. She underwent an uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy a week ago,
during which she received a prophylactic dose of cefotetan. Her past medical history is unremarkable,
and she denies any family history of genetic conditions. On examination, her temperature is 97.2°F
(36.7°C), blood pressure is 131/94 mmHg, pulse is 104/min, and respirations are 13/min. Physical
findings include jaundice and splenomegaly. Laboratory results show a hemoglobin level of 7.1 g/dL
(previously 13.2 g/dL one week ago). Additional tests reveal: Leukocyte count: 7,000/mm³ Platelet
count: 300,000/mm³ Mean corpuscular volume: 90 µm³ Reticulocyte count: 9% Lactate
dehydrogenase: 480 U/L (Normal: 140-280 U/L) Haptoglobin: 10 mg/dL (Normal: 41-165 mg/dL)
Indirect bilirubin: 2.7 mg/dL D-dimer: <250 ng/mL (Normal: <250 ng/mL) A peripheral blood smear
shows reticulocytosis and microspherocytes. Following appropriate initial management, which of the
following is the most suitable next diagnostic test? Answer Choices: (A) Cold agglutinin titer (B) Bone
marrow biopsy (C) Peripheral blood smear for Heinz bodies (D) Hemoglobin electrophoresis (E)
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) enzyme assay (F) Paroxysmal nocturnal
hemoglobinuria (PNH)-specific flow cytometry (G) Indirect Coombs test (H) Serum free hemoglobin
level (I) Direct Coombs test (J) Osmotic fragility test
 A. Serum free hemoglobin level
B. Peripheral blood smear for Heinz bodies
C. Indirect Coombs test
D. Osmotic fragility test
E. Hemoglobin electrophoresis
F. Bone marrow biopsy
G. Direct Coombs test
H. Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)-specific flow cytometry
I. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) enzyme assay
J. Cold agglutinin titer
